input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: § 7.2 conditions Customer's ability to engage any other provider on first disclosing and matching competing offers for Vendor — a right of first refusal that operates as de facto exclusivity/sole-supplier restraint on the customer, contrary to the preferred position of no exclusivity obligation on Customer. It is also inconsistent with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment, and it is reinforced by the § 2.1 three-year take-or-pay minimum (addressed under the minimum-commitment rule). Deletion is the minimal fix; a category- and 12-month-limited arrangement with automatic performance-failure exit is the fallback. Exclusivity running in Customer's favour is untouched.

proposal.summary: Delete § 7.2 disclose-and-match precondition on engaging another provider (de facto exclusivity)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the requirement to disclose and match competing offers before engaging another provider: conditioning our use of alternative suppliers on a right of first refusal is a de facto exclusivity commitment, which our playbook does not accept, and it contradicts § 12.3 (no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment). If Vendor needs something here, we can discuss a narrow arrangement limited to a defined service category for no more than 12 months that ends automatically if Vendor misses service levels or delivery dates.
